items.question: 什么是CSS？
answer_points: CSS是层叠样式表（Cascading Style Sheets）的缩写，用于描述HTML或XML文档的呈现方式。
CSS控制元素在屏幕、纸张、语音等媒体上的渲染。
CSS是开放网络的核心语言之一，由W3C规范标准化。
CSS不再有版本号（如CSS3），而是每个模块独立版本化。
follow_ups: CSS的层叠（cascade）规则是什么？

items.summary: CSS是用于描述文档呈现的样式表语言。
items.source_title: CSS: Cascading Style Sheets | MDN

items.question: 什么是JavaScript？
answer_points: JavaScript是一种轻量级的、解释型（或即时编译）的编程语言，具有一等函数。
它最著名的是作为Web页面的脚本语言，但也用于Node.js等非浏览器环境。
JavaScript是基于原型的、垃圾回收的、动态语言，支持命令式、函数式和面向对象编程范式。
JavaScript的标准是ECMAScript语言规范（ECMA-262）。
follow_ups: JavaScript和Java有什么区别？

items.summary: JavaScript是一种动态的、基于原型的编程语言，主要用于Web开发。

items.question: HTML中的<head>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <head>元素包含机器可读的元数据，如文档标题、脚本和样式表。
一个HTML文档只能有一个<head>元素。
<head>主要包含供机器处理的信息，而非人类可读内容。
常见的子元素包括<title>、<base>、<link>、<style>、<meta>、<script>等。

items.question: HTML中的<title>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <title>元素定义文档的标题，显示在浏览器的标题栏或标签页上。
它只包含文本，其中的HTML标签会被视为纯文本。
页面标题对SEO有重要影响，描述性标题通常效果更好。
建议标题长度不超过55-60个字符，重要内容前置。

items.question: HTML中的<body>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <body>元素表示HTML文档的内容，一个文档只能有一个<body>。
它包含所有可见的页面内容，如文本、图像、链接等。
<body>支持多种事件属性，如onload、onunload等。
一些属性如bgcolor、background已废弃，应使用CSS替代。

items.question: HTML中的<header>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <header>元素表示介绍性内容或导航辅助，通常包含标题、logo、搜索表单等。
当不嵌套在<section>等元素内时，它代表全局站点头部，具有banner地标角色。
当嵌套在<article>等元素内时，它失去地标角色，仅表示该部分的介绍性内容。
不能包含<header>或<footer>后代。

items.question: HTML中的<footer>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <footer>元素表示最近一个章节内容或章节根元素的页脚。
通常包含作者信息、版权数据或相关文档链接。
当最近的祖先章节内容是<body>时，<footer>应用于整个页面。
不能包含<header>或<footer>后代。
follow_ups: <footer>和<header>如何配合使用？

items.question: HTML中的<article>元素的作用是什么？
answer_points: <article>元素表示文档、页面或站点中独立的内容组合，可独立分发或复用。
常见示例包括论坛帖子、杂志文章、博客条目、产品卡片、用户评论等。
每个<article>通常应包含标题（<h1>-<h6>）。
嵌套的<article>表示与外部文章相关的内部文章，如博客评论。
follow_ups: <article>和<section>有什么区别？

items.question: What is the HTML <section> element and how should it be used?
answer_points: The <section> element represents a generic standalone section of a document that doesn't have a more specific semantic element.
Sections should always have a heading, with very few exceptions.
Use <article> for standalone atomic content, <aside> for tangential content, <main> for main content, and <div> for styling wrappers.
Each <section> should be identified, typically by including a heading (h1-h6) as a child.
follow_ups: When would you use <section> without a heading?
What is the difference between <section> and <div>?
items.summary: The <section> element is a generic sectioning element used when no more specific semantic element applies.
items.source_title: <section> HTML generic section element - HTML | MDN

What is the HTML

answer_points:
The

Paragraphs are block-level elements and automatically close if another block-level element is encountered before the closing tag.
The end tag may be omitted in certain contexts, such as when followed by another block-level element.

Use CSS margin properties to add space between paragraphs instead of empty

elements for accessibility.

element?

The

items.question: What is the HTML <div> element and when should it be used?
answer_points: The <div> element is a generic container for flow content with no inherent meaning.
It has no effect on content or layout until styled with CSS (e.g., Flexbox, Grid).
Use <div> only when no other semantic element (like <article>, <nav>, <section>) is appropriate.
It can be used to group content for styling or scripting purposes.
follow_ups: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?
Why should you prefer semantic elements over <div>?
items.summary: The <div> element is a non-semantic container used for styling and layout when no semantic element fits.
items.source_title: <div> HTML content division element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <span> element and how does it differ from <div>?
answer_points: The <span> element is a generic inline container for phrasing content, with no inherent meaning.
It is used to group elements for styling (via class or id) or attribute sharing (e.g., lang).
Unlike <div> (block-level), <span> is inline-level and does not start on a new line.
Use <span> only when no other semantic inline element is appropriate.
follow_ups: Can you nest <span> inside <div>?
What are some common use cases for <span>?
items.summary: The <span> element is an inline container for phrasing content, similar to <div> but inline.
items.source_title: <span> HTML content span element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML element and what are its key attributes?
answer_points: The element embeds an image into the document.
The src attribute specifies the image URL; alt provides a textual replacement for accessibility and fallback.
Use width and height to set intrinsic size and reduce layout shifts.
Responsive images can be achieved with srcset and sizes attributes.
Common image formats include JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP, and AVIF.
follow_ups: What is lazy loading and how does it apply to images?
How does the crossorigin attribute affect image loading?
items.summary: The element embeds images with required src and alt attributes, supporting responsive and accessible images.
items.source_title: HTML image embed element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <aside> element and how should it be used?
answer_points: The <aside> element represents content indirectly related to the main content, often displayed as sidebars or call-out boxes.
It should not be used for parenthesized text, as that is part of the main flow.
It is a sectioning element with an implicit ARIA role of complementary.
Common uses include related links, author bios, or tangential information.
follow_ups: What is the difference between <aside> and <section>?
Can <aside> be used inside <article>?
items.summary: The <aside> element marks content indirectly related to the main content, like sidebars or callouts.
items.source_title: <aside> HTML aside element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <audio> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <audio> element embeds sound content, with src attribute or <source> elements for multiple formats.
Key attributes include controls, autoplay, loop, muted, and preload.
Provide fallback content inside the element for unsupported browsers.
Use the Web Audio API for advanced audio manipulation or live streams via srcObject.
follow_ups: How do you handle multiple audio source formats?
What is the difference between preload and autoplay?
items.summary: The <audio> element embeds audio with support for multiple sources, controls, and fallback content.
items.source_title: <audio> HTML embed audio element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <canvas> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <canvas> element provides a bitmap area for drawing graphics via JavaScript (Canvas API or WebGL).
Set dimensions using width and height attributes; CSS sizing can distort the image.
Provide fallback content inside the element for unsupported browsers.
Use OffscreenCanvas for off-screen rendering in workers to avoid blocking the main thread.
Canvas content is not accessible; avoid using it for critical information without alternatives.
follow_ups: How do you draw on a canvas?
What are the limitations of canvas accessibility?
items.summary: The <canvas> element is used for dynamic graphics rendering via JavaScript, with accessibility limitations.
items.source_title: <canvas> HTML graphics canvas element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <details> element and how does it work?
answer_points: The <details> element creates a disclosure widget that can be toggled open/closed.
A <summary> element provides the label; without it, a default string is used.
The open attribute controls visibility; setting it to false still shows content because it's a Boolean attribute.
The name attribute groups multiple <details> elements so only one can be open at a time.
The toggle event fires when the state changes; events are coalesced if multiple changes occur quickly.
CSS can style the widget, but there is no built-in animation for the open/closed transition.
follow_ups: How can you programmatically open or close a <details> element?
What is the purpose of the name attribute on <details>?
How does the toggle event work and when is it dispatched?
items.summary: The <details> element creates a togglable disclosure widget with a <summary> label.
items.source_title: <details> HTML details disclosure element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <embed> element used for?
answer_points: The <embed> element embeds external content (e.g., from a plug-in) at a point in the document.
It requires src, type, width, and height attributes; width and height must be absolute CSS pixels.
Most modern browsers have deprecated plug-in support, so <embed> is generally not recommended.
Use the title attribute for accessibility to describe the embedded content.
The object-fit property does not affect <embed>; use object-position for positioning.
follow_ups: What are the alternatives to <embed> for embedding content?
Why is <embed> considered less accessible without a title attribute?
How does the type attribute affect the behavior of <embed>?
items.summary: The <embed> element embeds external content via plug-ins, but is deprecated in modern browsers.
items.source_title: <embed> HTML embed external content element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <nav> element and how should it be used?
answer_points: The <nav> element represents a section of a page with navigation links (within or to other documents).
It is intended for major navigation blocks; not all links need to be inside <nav>.
A document can have multiple <nav> elements; use aria-labelledby for accessibility.
Screen readers may use <nav> to skip navigation content.
The implicit ARIA role is navigation.
follow_ups: When should you use <nav> versus a <footer> with links?

items.summary: The <nav> element defines a navigation section for major links, aiding accessibility.

items.question: What is the HTML <search> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <search> element is a container for search or filtering controls and content.
It defines a search landmark, removing the need for role="search" on a <form>.
It is not for presenting search results; results should be in main content.
Quick search suggestions and links can be nested inside <search>.
Multiple <search> elements can exist; use title attributes to differentiate.

items.question: What is the HTML <output> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <output> element displays the result of a calculation or user action.
It has a for attribute listing IDs of input elements that contributed to the result.
The form attribute associates it with a <form> anywhere in the document.
Its value, name, and contents are not submitted with the form.
Many browsers treat it as an aria-live region, announcing changes to assistive technology.
follow_ups: How does the for attribute work with <output>?
Why is <output> not submitted with the form?
What is the implicit ARIA role of <output>?
items.summary: The <output> element shows calculation results or user action outcomes, with live region behavior.
items.source_title: <output> HTML output element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <progress> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <progress> element displays a progress bar indicating task completion.
It has max and value attributes; value must be between 0 and max (default max is 1).
Without a value attribute, the bar is indeterminate (ongoing activity with unknown duration).
Use <label> for accessible labeling; text between tags is fallback for old browsers.
The :indeterminate pseudo-class matches indeterminate progress bars.
follow_ups: How do you make a progress bar indeterminate after it had a value?
What is the difference between <progress> and <meter>?
How can you style the progress bar with CSS?
items.summary: The <progress> element shows task progress as a bar, with determinate and indeterminate states.
items.source_title: <progress> HTML progress indicator element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <video> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <video> element embeds a media player for video playback; can also be used for audio.
Use the src attribute or nested <source> elements to specify video sources.
Key attributes: controls, autoplay, loop, muted, poster, width, height, preload, loading.
Autoplay is blocked by modern browsers for unmuted audio; autoplay="false" does not work.
The loading="lazy" attribute defers loading until near viewport, affecting autoplay and preload.
Provide fallback content between tags for browsers that don't support <video>.
follow_ups: How do you provide multiple video formats for browser compatibility?
What is the difference between preload="none", "metadata", and "auto"?
How does the loading="lazy" attribute affect video behavior?
items.summary: The <video> element embeds video with controls, sources, and attributes for playback control.
items.source_title: <video> HTML video embed element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <ul> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <ul> element represents an unordered list of items, typically displayed with bullets.
Each list item is wrapped in an <li> element; <ul> can be nested inside <li>.
The deprecated type attribute (circle, disc, square) should be replaced with CSS list-style-type.
Use <ul> when the order of items is not meaningful; use <ol> when order matters.
The implicit ARIA role is list.
follow_ups: How do you nest lists in HTML?
What is the difference between <ul> and <ol>?
How can you change the bullet style using CSS?
items.summary: The <ul> element creates a bulleted list for items without a specific order.
items.source_title: <ul> HTML unordered list element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <ol> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <ol> element represents an ordered list, typically rendered as a numbered list.
It can contain <li> elements as list items.
Attributes include reversed, start, and type (a, A, i, I, 1).
Use CSS list-style-type instead of type attribute for styling.
Order matters; changing order changes meaning.
follow_ups: What is the difference between <ol> and <ul>?
How do you nest lists in HTML?
What is the start attribute and how does it work?
items.summary: The <ol> element defines an ordered list with numbering options.
items.source_title: <ol> HTML ordered list element - HTML | MDN

items.question: What is the HTML <li> element and how is it used?
answer_points: The <li> element represents an item in a list.
It must be contained in <ol>, <ul>, or <menu>.
In ordered lists, it displays with a counter; in unordered lists, with a bullet.
Attributes include value (for <ol>) and deprecated type.
The end tag can be omitted if followed by another <li> or no more content.
follow_ups: What is the value attribute on <li> used for?
Can <li> be used outside of <ol> or <ul>?
How does the implicit ARIA role work for <li>?
items.summary: The <li> element defines a list item within ordered or unordered lists.

items.question: How do you use HTML comments?
answer_points: HTML comments start with <!-- and end with -->, and are not visible on the page.
Comments can be single-line or multi-line, and can be placed before/after doctype, <html>, or as content of most elements except <script>, <style>, <title>, <textarea>.
Comments cannot be nested; the first --> closes the comment.
Comments are used for explanatory notes or to disable parts of the code.

items.question: How do you use HTML form validation and the Constraint Validation API?
answer_points: HTML5 introduced semantic input types and constraint validation attributes for client-side validation without JavaScript.
Basic constraints are declared via the type attribute (e.g., email, URL) and validation attributes like pattern, min, max, required, step, minlength, maxlength.
The Constraint Validation API provides methods like checkValidity() and reportValidity() for programmatic validation.
Complex constraints can be implemented using JavaScript and setCustomValidity() method.
Server-side validation is still necessary as client-side validation can be bypassed.
CSS pseudo-classes :valid, :invalid, :required, :optional can style form elements based on validation state.
